## Overview

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) publishes this document type approximately every two years for each member country and selected other states. It reviews macroeconomic developments, fiscal policy, and structural reforms. This card currently draws on twenty documents covering Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Spain.

## Use in the Rating Process

The document type feeds the minimal rating process and discretionary adjustments process for the following tasks:

- **[Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd) (C1\*)**: It provides growth forecasts and assessments of potential growth.
- **[Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) (C2\*)**: It supplies inflation projections and analysis of price competitiveness.
- **[Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd) (C3\*)**: It offers fiscal projections and assessments of debt sustainability.
- **[Outlook Factors](../parameters/outlook-factors.qmd) (R7\*)**: It provides context on structural challenges, demographic pressures, and political risks.

## Methods

- The OECD uses its Economic Outlook database for short-term projections and its Long-Term Model for long-term scenarios. Potential GDP is estimated using structural methods. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26">ⓘ</button>
- Long-run fiscal projections assume current tax and spending policies unless specified otherwise. The "Consolidation scenario" assumes the primary budget surplus reaches 0.6% of GDP by 2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses historical GDP growth data and potential growth estimates based on production function approaches, accounting for capital stock, labour force, and total factor productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD assesses fiscal capacity using the structural primary balance, adjusted for the output gap and one-off measures. The analysis includes long-term projections of ageing-related expenditures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD builds the gross financing need from the debt stock, short-term debt, weighted average maturity, and deficit. It cross-checks against published data on government debt and interest payments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD projects that without policy adjustments, the government debt ratio would rise due to current budget deficits and ageing pressures. A consolidation scenario assumes an improvement in the primary fiscal balance by 0.5% of GDP per year over 2027-2033. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD notes that debt dynamics are currently favourable as expected nominal growth is well above interest rates on government debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 53" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 53">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses its Economic Outlook database for growth projections and historical data. Potential GDP growth is estimated to decline from over 4% in 2024 to 0.3% in 2070 due to demographic headwinds. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal sustainability is assessed using stylized debt scenarios. The "Current policies" scenario projects debt rising to 90% of GDP by 2040. The "Fiscal rules scenario" assumes a structural primary budget deficit of 0.4% is reached in 2028, stabilizing debt at around 55% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- Debt metrics include both Maastricht-defined gross debt and broader general government gross debt. The document highlights the importance of monitoring contingent liabilities from SOEs and climate risks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses its Economic Outlook Database for short-term projections (2025-2026) and the OECD Long-Term Model for medium- and long-term simulations (up to 2050). The long-term model incorporates scenarios for employment reforms, population growth, and fiscal consolidation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD estimates the structural deficit and projects the general government fiscal balance based on policy assumptions, including the impact of recent tax changes and defense spending increases. The underlying government primary balance is used as a key indicator of fiscal effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- Debt projections are based on gross general government debt and Maastricht definition debt. The OECD simulations assess the long-term trajectory of debt under different policy and demographic scenarios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses OECD Economic Outlook database projections for real GDP growth, unemployment, and inflation to assess growth momentum and potential output. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- The analysis relies on OECD Long-Term Model simulations and European Commission ageing projections to assess debt sustainability and the impact of structural reforms on the primary balance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- Debt trajectories are projected using gross debt data from the OECD Economic Outlook database, incorporating assumptions about interest rates, growth, and discretionary fiscal measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses simulations to estimate that structural reforms could raise potential GDP per capita growth by about 0.8 percentage points per year until 2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD conducts simulations using the OECD Long-term Model to assess fiscal sustainability. Issuing public debt to finance additional defence and infrastructure spending, while using the structural deficit limit, would increase the debt-to-GDP ratio to about 81% by 2045. If rising spending pressures due to ageing are not addressed, debt would increase to about 128% of GDP in 2045. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 38-39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 38-39">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses potential GDP growth estimates to assess structural growth trends. It projects potential growth at 2.2–2.3% for 2024–2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes primary balance projections and debt sustainability scenarios, assuming primary surpluses of around 2% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD assesses refinancing risks by examining the weighted average maturity of public debt (approx. 19 years) and the share of official lending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses its Long-Term Model to project potential growth, accounting for policy reforms. It estimates that reforms in institutional quality, labor force participation, and R&D could raise GDP by 3.9% over 10 years and 11.9% over 25 years relative to baseline. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes debt sustainability under alternative fiscal and structural policy scenarios, assuming a long-term interest rate stabilizing at 4.2% and a weighted average interest rate of 3.2%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses Modified Domestic Demand (MDD) and Modified Gross National Income (GNI*) to capture underlying domestic dynamics, excluding volatile multinational transactions such as on-shored intellectual property and aircraft leasing. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal variables, such as public debt and budget balances, are assessed as a share of GNI* to provide a better assessment of the fiscal situation, removing globalization-related distortions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is analyzed under current policies, fiscal reforms, and fiscal plus structural reforms scenarios, projecting debt-to-GNI* ratios up to 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses historical GDP growth data and projections for 2025–2026. It notes that potential GDP growth is expected to decline due to slower labour and productivity growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD reports HICP inflation and GDP deflator figures. It notes that wage growth has fueled inflation and weakened competitiveness. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD projects the general government balance and underlying fiscal balance, highlighting the need for fiscal adjustment to address ageing-related costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD reports general government gross debt and net financial liabilities. It notes the low level of public debt but projects an increase in the coming years. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses its Economic Outlook Database for growth projections and historical data. Potential GDP growth is estimated to decline from over 4% in 2024 to 0.3% in 2070 due to demographic headwinds. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 89">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD projects that gross public debt remains stable until the late 2040s but rises rapidly thereafter due to aging-related expenditure, particularly pensions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD recommends adopting a national net spending rule to anchor fiscal policy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD identifies the pension system's sustainability as a major long-term risk, projecting pension expenditure to rise from 9.4% of GDP in 2024 to 17.5% in 2070 without reform. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The transition to green growth will have a net negative impact on the budget balance, estimated at around 2% of GDP by 2050, primarily due to lower fuel revenues. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides historical real GDP growth data and forecasts for 2025 and 2026. It also includes estimates for potential GDP growth and the output gap, which are relevant for assessing the growth drift and volatility parameters. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) for the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd) and provides forecasts. [oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 12; <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 2" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 2">ⓘ</button>8]
- The document reports the general government fiscal balance, primary balance, and gross debt as percentages of GDP. [oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 12; <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 2" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 2">ⓘ</button>8]
- The OECD uses potential GDP estimates to assess output gaps and structural growth trends. Potential GDP is projected to decline from 2.4% in 2024 to 1.9% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD analyzes primary balances and structural deficits to assess fiscal sustainability. It highlights the gap between the current primary balance and the required surplus to stabilize debt at target levels. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is assessed using Maastricht-defined gross debt and net debt metrics, alongside projections of interest costs and growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD assesses growth potential through labour market participation, skills mismatches, and demographic trends. It highlights that closing gender gaps could raise GDP per capita by 5% by 2060. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 80" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 80">ⓘ</button>
- The document discusses fiscal efforts in social housing and housing allowances, noting low spending relative to [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) averages and poor targeting. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 130" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 130">ⓘ</button>
- The document addresses contingent liabilities from low insurance coverage for climate risks and the inefficiency of property taxation in capturing value from vacant and underused assets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 98" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 98">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses macroeconomic projections to assess growth trends, noting the impact of fiscal expansion and external uncertainty on GDP growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The survey evaluates fiscal sustainability through stylised debt scenarios, projecting debt-to-GDP ratios under different policy assumptions, including pension reforms and defence spending increases. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses OECD Economic Outlook projections for real GDP growth, distinguishing between historical data and forecasts for 2025-2027. It also discusses potential GDP growth and the output gap, noting that the output gap is almost closed, supporting the case for fiscal consolidation <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34">ⓘ</button>.
- The analysis relies on Maastricht definition for debt and deficit, as well as OECD calculations for long-term fiscal sustainability. It incorporates scenarios based on AIReF’s projections for aging costs and pension sustainability <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 46">ⓘ</button>.
- Inflation projections are based on the OECD Economic Outlook database, tracking headline and core consumer price index changes <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD uses illustrative simulations to assess fiscal sustainability. It estimates that combining fiscal adjustment with structural reforms boosting employment could reduce the required primary balance improvement from 5.1% of GDP to 2.4% of GDP to bring debt to 40% of GDP within two decades <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 28-29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 28-29">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD employs long-term modeling to estimate the impact of demographic changes and structural reforms on potential GDP growth. It projects that ageing could reduce the employment share of the population by 4 percentage points over 2025-2060 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 31">ⓘ</button>.
- The OECD analyzes the effectiveness of the debt brake using a fiscal reaction function estimated over 1995-2024. It finds that the primary balance became more stabilising in response to debt levels after EU accession negotiations began, but not after the introduction of the debt brake <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 50" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 50">ⓘ</button>.
